entries.originalText: Our apostles also knew, through our Lord Jesus Christ, that there would be strife on account of the office of the episcopate.
entries.modernizedText: Our apostles also knew, through our Lord Jesus Christ, that there would be strife on account of the office of the episcopate.

entries.originalText: For this reason, therefore, inasmuch as they had obtained a perfect fore-knowledge of this, they appointed those [ministers] already mentioned, and afterwards gave instructions, that when these should fall asleep, other approved men should succeed them in their ministry.
entries.modernizedText: For this reason, therefore, since they had obtained a perfect foreknowledge of this, they appointed those [ministers] already mentioned, and afterward gave instructions that when these should fall asleep, other approved men should succeed them in their ministry.

entries.originalText: We are of opinion, therefore, that those appointed by them, or afterwards by other eminent men, with the consent of the whole church, and who have blamelessly served the flock of Christ, in a humble, peaceable, and disinterested spirit, and have for a long time possessed the good opinion of all, cannot be justly dismissed from the ministry.
entries.modernizedText: We are of the opinion, therefore, that those appointed by them, or afterward by other eminent men, with the consent of the whole church, and who have blamelessly served the flock of Christ in a humble, peaceful, and disinterested spirit, and have for a long time possessed the good opinion of all, cannot justly be dismissed from the ministry.

entries.originalText: For our sin will not be small, if we eject from the episcopate those who have blamelessly and holily fulfilled its duties.
entries.modernizedText: For our sin will not be small if we eject from the episcopate those who have blamelessly and faithfully fulfilled its duties.

entries.originalText: Blessed are those presbyters who, having finished their course before now, have obtained a fruitful and perfect departure [from this world]; for they have no fear lest any one deprive them of the place now appointed them.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed are those presbyters who, having finished their course before now, have obtained a fruitful and perfect departure [from this world]; for they have no fear that anyone will deprive them of the place now appointed to them.

entries.originalText: But we see that ye have removed some men of excellent behaviour from the ministry, which they fulfilled blamelessly and with honour.
entries.modernizedText: But we see that you have removed some men of excellent behavior from the ministry, which they fulfilled blamelessly and with honor.

entries.originalText: Ye are fond of contention, brethren, and full of zeal about things which do not pertain to salvation.
entries.modernizedText: You are fond of contention, brethren, and full of zeal about things that do not pertain to salvation.

entries.originalText: Look carefully into the Scriptures, which are the true utterances of the Holy Spirit.
entries.modernizedText: Look carefully into the Scriptures, which are the true utterances of the Holy Spirit.

entries.originalText: Observe that nothing of an unjust or counterfeit character is written in them.
entries.modernizedText: Observe that nothing unjust or counterfeit is written in them.

entries.originalText: There you will not find that the righteous were cast off by men who themselves were holy.
entries.modernizedText: There you will not find that the righteous were cast off by men who themselves were holy.

entries.originalText: The righteous were indeed persecuted, but only by the wicked.
entries.modernizedText: The righteous were indeed persecuted, but only by the wicked.

entries.originalText: They were cast into prison, but only by the unholy; they were stoned, but only by transgressors; they were slain, but only by the accursed, and such as had conceived an unrighteous envy against them.
entries.modernizedText: They were cast into prison, but only by the unholy; they were stoned, but only by transgressors; they were slain, but only by the accursed and those who had conceived an unrighteous envy against them.

entries.originalText: Exposed to such sufferings, they endured them gloriously.
entries.modernizedText: Exposed to such sufferings, they endured them gloriously.

entries.originalText: For what shall we say, brethren?
entries.modernizedText: For what shall we say, brethren?

entries.originalText: Was Daniel cast into the den of lions by such as feared God?
entries.modernizedText: Was Daniel cast into the den of lions by those who feared God?

entries.originalText: Were Ananias, and Azarias, and Michael shut up in a furnace of fire by those who observed the great and glorious worship of the Most High?
entries.modernizedText: Were Ananias, Azarias, and Michael shut up in a furnace of fire by those who observed the great and glorious worship of the Most High?

entries.originalText: Far from us be such a thought!
entries.modernizedText: Far from us be such a thought!

entries.originalText: Who, then, were they that did such things?
entries.modernizedText: Who, then, were they who did such things?

entries.originalText: The hateful, and those full of all wickedness, were roused to such a pitch of fury, that they inflicted torture on those who served God with a holy and blameless purpose [of heart], not knowing that the Most High is the Defender and Protector of all such as with a pure conscience venerate His all-excellent name; to whom be glory for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: The hateful and those full of all wickedness were roused to such a pitch of fury that they inflicted torture on those who served God with a holy and blameless purpose [of heart], not knowing that the Most High is the Defender and Protector of all who venerate His all-excellent name with a pure conscience; to Him be glory forever and ever.

entries.originalText: But they who with confidence endured [these things] are now heirs of glory and honour, and have been exalted and made illustrious by God in their memorial for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: But those who confidently endured [these things] are now heirs of glory and honor, and have been exalted and made illustrious by God in their memorial forever and ever.

entries.originalText: Such examples, therefore, brethren, it is right that we should follow; since it is written, “Cleave to the holy, for those that cleave to them shall [themselves] be made holy.”
entries.modernizedText: Such examples, therefore, brethren, it is right that we should follow, since it is written, “Cleave to the holy, for those who cleave to them shall [themselves] be made holy.”

entries.originalText: And again, in another place, [the Scripture] saith, “With a harmless man thou shalt prove thyself harmless, and with an elect man thou shalt be elect, and with a perverse man thou shalt show thyself perverse.”
entries.modernizedText: And again, in another place, [the Scripture] says, “With a harmless man you shall prove yourself harmless, and with an elect man you shall be elect, and with a perverse man you shall show yourself perverse.”

entries.originalText: Let us cleave, therefore, to the innocent and righteous, since these are the elect of God.
entries.modernizedText: Let us cleave, therefore, to the innocent and righteous, since these are the elect of God.

entries.originalText: Why are there strifes, and tumults, and divisions, and schisms, and wars among you?
entries.modernizedText: Why are there strifes, tumults, divisions, schisms, and wars among you?

entries.originalText: Have we not [all] one God and one Christ?
entries.modernizedText: Do we not [all] have one God and one Christ?

entries.originalText: Is there not one Spirit of grace poured out upon us?
entries.modernizedText: Is there not one Spirit of grace poured out upon us?

entries.originalText: And have we not one calling in Christ?
entries.modernizedText: And do we not have one calling in Christ?

entries.originalText: Why do we divide and tear in pieces the members of Christ, and raise up strife against our own body, and have reached such a height of madness as to forget that “we are members one of another?”
entries.modernizedText: Why do we divide and tear apart the members of Christ, raise up strife against our own body, and reach such a height of madness as to forget that “we are members of one another?”

entries.originalText: Remember the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, how He said, “Woe to that man [by whom offences come]!
entries.modernizedText: Remember the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, how He said, “Woe to that man [by whom offenses come]!

entries.originalText: It were better for him that he had never been born, than that he should cast a stumbling-block before one of my elect.
entries.modernizedText: It would be better for him if he had never been born than that he should cast a stumbling block before one of my elect.

entries.originalText: Yea, it were better for him that a millstone should be hung about [his neck], and he should be sunk in the depths of the sea, than that he should cast a stumbling-block before one of my little ones.”
entries.modernizedText: Yes, it would be better for him if a millstone were hung around [his neck] and he were sunk in the depths of the sea than that he should cast a stumbling block before one of my little ones.”

entries.originalText: Your schism has subverted [the faith of] many, has discouraged many, has given rise to doubt in many, and has caused grief to us all.
entries.modernizedText: Your schism has subverted [the faith of] many, discouraged many, given rise to doubt in many, and caused grief to us all.

entries.originalText: And still your sedition continueth.
entries.modernizedText: And still your sedition continues.

entries.originalText: Take up the epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul.
entries.modernizedText: Take up the epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul.

entries.originalText: What did he write to you at the time when the gospel first began to be preached?
entries.modernizedText: What did he write to you at the time when the gospel first began to be preached?

entries.originalText: Truly, under the inspiration of the Spirit, he wrote to you concerning himself, and Cephas, and Apollos, because even then parties had been formed among you.
entries.modernizedText: Truly, under the inspiration of the Spirit, he wrote to you concerning himself, Cephas, and Apollos, because even then parties had been formed among you.

entries.originalText: But that inclination for one above another entailed less guilt upon you, inasmuch as your partialities were then shown towards apostles, already of high reputation, and towards a man whom they had approved.
entries.modernizedText: But that preference for one over another brought less guilt upon you, since your partialities were then shown toward apostles already of high reputation and toward a man whom they had approved.

entries.originalText: But now reflect who those are that have perverted you, and lessened the renown of your far-famed brotherly love.
entries.modernizedText: But now consider who those are who have perverted you and diminished the renown of your far-famed brotherly love.

entries.originalText: It is disgraceful, beloved, yea, highly disgraceful, and unworthy of your Christian profession, that such a thing should be heard of as that the most stedfast and ancient church of the Corinthians should, on account of one or two persons, engage in sedition against its presbyters.
entries.modernizedText: It is disgraceful, beloved, yes, highly disgraceful and unworthy of your Christian profession, that such a thing should be heard of as the most steadfast and ancient church of the Corinthians engaging in sedition against its presbyters on account of one or two persons.

entries.originalText: And this rumour has reached not only us, but those also who are unconnected with us; so that, through your infatuation, the name of the Lord is blasphemed, while danger is also brought upon yourselves.
entries.modernizedText: And this rumor has reached not only us but also those who are unconnected with us, so that through your infatuation the name of the Lord is blasphemed, while danger is also brought upon yourselves.

entries.originalText: Let us therefore, with all haste, put an end to this [state of things]; and let us fall down before the Lord, and beseech Him with tears, that He would mercifully be reconciled to us, and restore us to our former seemly and holy practice of brotherly love.
entries.modernizedText: Let us therefore, with all haste, put an end to this [state of things]; and let us fall down before the Lord and beseech Him with tears that He would mercifully be reconciled to us and restore us to our former seemly and holy practice of brotherly love.

entries.originalText: For [such conduct] is the gate of righteousness, which is set open for the attainment of life, as it is written, “Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will go in by them, and will praise the Lord: this is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter in by it.”
entries.modernizedText: For [such conduct] is the gate of righteousness, which is set open for the attainment of life, as it is written, “Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will go in by them and will praise the Lord: this is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter in by it.”

entries.originalText: Although, therefore, many gates have been set open, yet this gate of righteousness is that gate in Christ by which blessed are all they that have entered in and have directed their way in holiness and righteousness, doing all things without disorder.
entries.modernizedText: Although, therefore, many gates have been set open, this gate of righteousness is the gate in Christ by which all who have entered and directed their way in holiness and righteousness are blessed, doing all things without disorder.

entries.originalText: Let a man be faithful: let him be powerful in the utterance of knowledge; let him be wise in judging of words; let him be pure in all his deeds; yet the more he seems to be superior to others [in these respects], the more humble-minded ought he to be, and to seek the common good of all, and not merely his own advantage.
entries.modernizedText: Let a man be faithful; let him be powerful in the utterance of knowledge; let him be wise in judging words; let him be pure in all his deeds. Yet the more he seems to be superior to others [in these respects], the more humble-minded he ought to be, seeking the common good of all and not merely his own advantage.

entries.originalText: Let him who has love in Christ keep the commandments of Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Let him who has love in Christ keep the commandments of Christ.

entries.originalText: Who can describe the [blessed] bond of the love of God?
entries.modernizedText: Who can describe the [blessed] bond of the love of God?

entries.originalText: What man is able to tell the excellence of its beauty, as it ought to be told?
entries.modernizedText: What man is able to tell the excellence of its beauty as it ought to be told?

entries.originalText: The height to which love exalts is unspeakable.
entries.modernizedText: The height to which love exalts us is unspeakable.

entries.originalText: Love unites us to God.
entries.modernizedText: Love unites us to God.

entries.originalText: Love covers a multitude of sins.
entries.modernizedText: Love covers a multitude of sins.

entries.originalText: Love beareth all things, is long-suffering in all things.
entries.modernizedText: Love bears all things and is patient in all things.

entries.originalText: There is nothing base, nothing arrogant in love.
entries.modernizedText: There is nothing base and nothing arrogant in love.

entries.originalText: Love admits of no schisms: love gives rise to no seditions: love does all things in harmony.
entries.modernizedText: Love admits of no schisms; love gives rise to no seditions; love does all things in harmony.

entries.originalText: By love have all the elect of God been made perfect; without love nothing is well-pleasing to God.
entries.modernizedText: By love all the elect of God have been made perfect; without love nothing is pleasing to God.

entries.originalText: In love has the Lord taken us to Himself.
entries.modernizedText: In love the Lord has taken us to Himself.

entries.originalText: On account of the love He bore us, Jesus Christ our Lord gave His blood for us by the will of God; His flesh for our flesh, and His soul for our souls.
entries.modernizedText: Because of the love He bore us, Jesus Christ our Lord gave His blood for us by the will of God; His flesh for our flesh and His soul for our souls.

entries.originalText: Ye see, beloved, how great and wonderful a thing is love, and that there is no declaring its perfection.
entries.modernizedText: You see, beloved, how great and wonderful a thing love is, and that its perfection cannot be declared.

entries.originalText: Who is fit to be found in it, except such as God has vouchsafed to render so?
entries.modernizedText: Who is fit to be found in it except those whom God has graciously made so?

entries.originalText: Let us pray, therefore, and implore of His mercy, that we may live blameless in love, free from all human partialities for one above another.
entries.modernizedText: Let us pray, therefore, and implore His mercy, that we may live blameless in love, free from all human partialities for one above another.

entries.originalText: All the generations from Adam even unto this day have passed away; but those who, through the grace of God, have been made perfect in love, now possess a place among the godly, and shall be made manifest at the revelation of the kingdom of Christ.
entries.modernizedText: All the generations from Adam even to this day have passed away; but those who, through the grace of God, have been made perfect in love now possess a place among the godly and shall be made manifest at the revelation of the kingdom of Christ.

entries.originalText: For it is written, “Enter into thy secret chambers for a little time, until my wrath and fury pass away; and I will remember a propitious day, and will raise you up out of your graves.”
entries.modernizedText: For it is written, “Enter into your secret chambers for a little while, until my wrath and fury pass away; and I will remember a favorable day, and will raise you up out of your graves.”

entries.originalText: Blessed are we, beloved, if we keep the commandments of God in the harmony of love; that so through love our sins may be forgiven us.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed are we, beloved, if we keep the commandments of God in the harmony of love, so that through love our sins may be forgiven us.

entries.originalText: For it is written, “Blessed are they whose transgressions are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
entries.modernizedText: For it is written, “Blessed are those whose transgressions are forgiven and whose sins are covered.

entries.originalText: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not impute to him, and in whose mouth there is no guile.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not impute to him and in whose mouth there is no guile.

entries.originalText: This blessedness cometh upon those who have been chosen by God through Jesus Christ our Lord; to whom be glory for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: This blessedness comes upon those who have been chosen by God through Jesus Christ our Lord; to Him be glory forever and ever.

entries.originalText: Let us therefore implore forgiveness for all those transgressions which through any [suggestion] of the adversary we have committed.
entries.modernizedText: Let us therefore implore forgiveness for all those transgressions that through any [suggestion] of the adversary we have committed.

entries.originalText: And these who have been the leaders of sedition and disagreement ought to have respect to the common hope.
entries.modernizedText: And those who have been the leaders of sedition and disagreement ought to have regard for the common hope.

entries.originalText: For such as live in fear and love would rather that they themselves than their neighbours should be involved in suffering.
entries.modernizedText: For those who live in fear and love would rather that they themselves, rather than their neighbors, should be involved in suffering.

entries.originalText: And they prefer to bear blame themselves, rather than that the concord which has been well and piously handed down to us should suffer.
entries.modernizedText: And they prefer to bear blame themselves rather than let the concord that has been well and piously handed down to us suffer.

entries.originalText: For it is better that a man should acknowledge his transgressions than that he should harden his heart, as the hearts of those were hardened who stirred up sedition against Moses the servant of God, and whose condemnation was made manifest [unto all].
entries.modernizedText: For it is better that a man should acknowledge his transgressions than harden his heart, as the hearts of those who stirred up sedition against Moses the servant of God were hardened, and whose condemnation was made manifest [to all].

entries.originalText: For they went down alive into Hades, and death swallowed them up.
entries.modernizedText: For they went down alive into Hades, and death swallowed them up.

entries.originalText: Pharaoh with his army and all the princes of Egypt, and the chariots with their riders, were sunk in the depths of the Red Sea, and perished, for no other reason than that their foolish hearts were hardened, after so many signs and wonders had been wrought in the land of Egypt by Moses the servant of God.
entries.modernizedText: Pharaoh with his army and all the princes of Egypt, and the chariots with their riders, were sunk in the depths of the Red Sea and perished for no other reason than that their foolish hearts were hardened, after so many signs and wonders had been performed in the land of Egypt by Moses the servant of God.

entries.originalText: The Lord, brethren, stands in need of nothing; and He desires nothing of any one except that confession be made to Him.
entries.modernizedText: The Lord, brethren, stands in need of nothing; and He desires nothing from anyone except that confession be made to Him.

entries.originalText: For, says the elect David, “I will confess unto the Lord; and that will please Him more than a young bullock that hath horns and hoofs.
entries.modernizedText: For, says the elect David, “I will confess to the Lord; and that will please Him more than a young bullock that has horns and hooves.

entries.originalText: Let the poor see it, and be glad.”
entries.modernizedText: Let the poor see it and be glad.”

entries.originalText: And again he saith, “Offer unto God the sacrifice of praise, and pay thy vows unto the Most High.
entries.modernizedText: And again he says, “Offer to God the sacrifice of praise, and pay Your vows to the Most High.

entries.originalText: And call upon me in the day of thy trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.”
entries.modernizedText: And call upon me in the day of Your trouble: I will deliver You, and You shall glorify me.”

entries.originalText: For “the sacrifice of God is a broken spirit.”
entries.modernizedText: For “the sacrifice of God is a broken spirit.”

entries.originalText: Ye understand, beloved, ye understand well the sacred Scriptures, and ye have looked very earnestly into the oracles of God.
entries.modernizedText: You understand, beloved, you understand the sacred Scriptures well, and you have looked very earnestly into the oracles of God.

entries.originalText: Call then these things to your remembrance.
entries.modernizedText: Call these things, then, to your remembrance.

entries.originalText: When Moses went up into the mount, and abode there, with fasting and humiliation, forty days and forty nights, the Lord said unto him, “Moses, Moses, get thee down quickly from hence; for thy people whom thou didst bring out of the land of Egypt have committed iniquity.
entries.modernizedText: When Moses went up onto the mountain and remained there with fasting and humiliation for forty days and forty nights, the Lord said to him, “Moses, Moses, get down quickly from here; for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have committed iniquity.

entries.originalText: They have speedily departed from the way in which I commanded them to walk, and have made to themselves molten images.”
entries.modernizedText: They have quickly departed from the way in which I commanded them to walk and have made molten images for themselves.”

entries.originalText: And the Lord said unto him, “I have spoken to thee once and again, saying, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiff-necked people: let me destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make thee a great and wonderful nation, and one much more numerous than this.”
entries.modernizedText: And the Lord said to him, “I have spoken to you once and again, saying, I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people. Let me destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven, and I will make you a great and wonderful nation, much more numerous than this.”

entries.originalText: But Moses said, “Far be it from Thee, Lord: pardon the sin of this people; else blot me also out of the book of the living.”
entries.modernizedText: But Moses said, “Far be it from You, Lord; pardon the sin of this people, or else blot me also out of the book of the living.”

entries.originalText: O marvellous love!
entries.modernizedText: O marvelous love!

entries.originalText: O insuperable perfection!
entries.modernizedText: O unsurpassable perfection!

entries.originalText: The servant speaks freely to his Lord, and asks forgiveness for the people, or begs that he himself might perish along with them.
entries.modernizedText: The servant speaks freely to his Lord and asks forgiveness for the people, or begs that he himself might perish along with them.

entries.originalText: Who then among you is noble-minded? who compassionate? who full of love?
entries.modernizedText: Who, then, among you is noble-minded? Who is compassionate? Who is full of love?

entries.originalText: Let him declare, “If on my account sedition and disagreement and schisms have arisen, I will depart, I will go away whithersoever ye desire, and I will do whatever the majority commands; only let the flock of Christ live on terms of peace with the presbyters set over it.”
entries.modernizedText: Let him declare, “If on my account sedition, disagreement, and schisms have arisen, I will depart; I will go wherever you desire, and I will do whatever the majority commands. Only let the flock of Christ live in peace with the presbyters set over it.”

entries.originalText: He that acts thus shall procure to himself great glory in the Lord; and every place will welcome him.
entries.modernizedText: He who acts thus will procure great glory for himself in the Lord, and every place will welcome him.

entries.originalText: For “the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof.”
entries.modernizedText: For “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”

entries.originalText: These things they who live a godly life that is never to be repented of, both have done and always will do.
entries.modernizedText: Those who live a godly life that is never to be repented of have both done these things and always will do them.

entries.originalText: To bring forward some examples from among the heathen: Many kings and princes, in times of pestilence, when they had been instructed by an oracle, have given themselves up to death, in order that by their own blood they might deliver their fellow-citizens [from destruction].
entries.modernizedText: To bring forward some examples from among the heathen: many kings and princes, in times of pestilence, when they had been instructed by an oracle, have given themselves up to death so that by their own blood they might deliver their fellow citizens [from destruction].

entries.originalText: Many have gone forth from their own cities, that so sedition might be brought to an end within them.
entries.modernizedText: Many have gone forth from their own cities so that sedition might be brought to an end within them.

entries.originalText: We know many among ourselves who have given themselves up to bonds, in order that they might ransom others.
entries.modernizedText: We know many among ourselves who have given themselves up to bonds so that they might ransom others.

entries.originalText: Many, too, have surrendered themselves to slavery, that with the price which they received for themselves, they might provide food for others.
entries.modernizedText: Many, too, have surrendered themselves to slavery so that with the price they received for themselves they might provide food for others.

entries.originalText: Many women also, being strengthened by the grace of God, have performed numerous manly exploits.
entries.modernizedText: Many women also, strengthened by the grace of God, have performed numerous courageous deeds.

entries.originalText: The blessed Judith, when her city was besieged, asked of the elders permission to go forth into the camp of the strangers; and, exposing herself to danger, she went out for the love which she bare to her country and people then besieged; and the Lord delivered Holofernes into the hands of a woman.
entries.modernizedText: The blessed Judith, when her city was besieged, asked the elders for permission to go into the camp of the strangers; and, exposing herself to danger, she went out because of the love she bore for her country and the people then besieged; and the Lord delivered Holofernes into the hands of a woman.

entries.originalText: Esther also, being perfect in faith, exposed herself to no less danger, in order to deliver the twelve tribes of Israel from impending destruction.
entries.modernizedText: Esther also, being perfect in faith, exposed herself to no less danger in order to deliver the twelve tribes of Israel from impending destruction.

entries.originalText: For with fasting and humiliation she entreated the everlasting God, who seeth all things; and He, perceiving the humility of her spirit, delivered the people for whose sake she had encountered peril.
entries.modernizedText: For with fasting and humiliation she entreated the everlasting God, who sees all things; and He, perceiving the humility of her spirit, delivered the people for whose sake she had faced danger.

entries.originalText: Let us then also pray for those who have fallen into any sin, that meekness and humility may be given to them, so that they may submit, not unto us, but to the will of God.
entries.modernizedText: Let us then also pray for those who have fallen into any sin, that meekness and humility may be given to them, so that they may submit not to us but to the will of God.

entries.originalText: For in this way they shall secure a fruitful and perfect remembrance from us, with sympathy for them, both in our prayers to God, and our mention of them to the saints.
entries.modernizedText: For in this way they shall secure a fruitful and perfect remembrance from us, with sympathy for them both in our prayers to God and in our mention of them to the saints.

entries.originalText: Let us receive correction, beloved, on account of which no one should feel displeased.
entries.modernizedText: Let us receive correction, beloved, at which no one should be displeased.

entries.originalText: Those exhortations by which we admonish one another are both good [in themselves], and highly profitable, for they tend to unite us to the will of God.
entries.modernizedText: Those exhortations by which we admonish one another are both good [in themselves] and highly profitable, for they tend to unite us to the will of God.

entries.originalText: For thus saith the holy Word: “The Lord hath severely chastened me, yet hath not given me over to death.”
entries.modernizedText: For thus says the holy Word: “The Lord has severely chastened me, yet has not given me over to death.”

entries.originalText: “For whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom He receiveth.”
entries.modernizedText: “For whom the Lord loves He chastens, and scourges every son whom He receives.”

entries.originalText: “The righteous,” saith it, “shall chasten me in mercy, and reprove me; but let not the oil of sinners make fat my head.”
entries.modernizedText: “The righteous,” it says, “shall chasten me in mercy and reprove me; but let not the oil of sinners make my head fat.”

entries.originalText: And again he saith, “Blessed is the man whom the Lord reproveth, and reject not thou the warning of the Almighty.
entries.modernizedText: And again he says, “Blessed is the man whom the Lord reproves, and do not reject the warning of the Almighty.

entries.originalText: For He causes sorrow, and again restores [to gladness]; He woundeth, and His hands make whole.
entries.modernizedText: For He causes sorrow and again restores [to gladness]; He wounds, and His hands make whole.

entries.originalText: He shall deliver thee in six troubles, yea, in the seventh no evil shall touch thee.
entries.modernizedText: He shall deliver you in six troubles; yes, in the seventh no evil shall touch you.

entries.originalText: In famine He shall rescue thee from death, and in war He shall free thee from the power of the sword.
entries.modernizedText: In famine He shall rescue you from death, and in war He shall free you from the power of the sword.

entries.originalText: From the scourge of the tongue will He hide thee, and thou shalt not fear when evil cometh.
entries.modernizedText: From the scourge of the tongue He will hide you, and you shall not fear when evil comes.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt laugh at the unrighteous and the wicked, and shalt not be afraid of the beasts of the field.
entries.modernizedText: You shall laugh at the unrighteous and the wicked, and shall not be afraid of the beasts of the field.

entries.originalText: For the wild beasts shall be at peace with thee: then shalt thou know that thy house shall be in peace, and the habitation of thy tabernacle shall not fail.
entries.modernizedText: For the wild beasts shall be at peace with you; then you shall know that your house shall be in peace, and the habitation of your tabernacle shall not fail.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thy children like the grass of the field.
entries.modernizedText: You shall also know that your seed shall be great, and your children like the grass of the field.

entries.originalText: And thou shalt come to the grave like ripened corn which is reaped in its season, or like a heap of the threshing-floor which is gathered together at the proper time.”
entries.modernizedText: And you shall come to the grave like ripened grain that is reaped in its season, or like a heap from the threshing floor that is gathered together at the proper time.”

entries.originalText: Ye see, beloved, that “protection is afforded to those that are chastened of the Lord; for since God is good, He corrects us, that we may be admonished” by His holy chastisement.
entries.modernizedText: You see, beloved, that “protection is afforded to those who are chastened by the Lord; for since God is good, He corrects us, that we may be admonished” by His holy chastisement.

entries.originalText: Ye therefore, who laid the foundation of this sedition, submit yourselves to the presbyters, and receive correction so as to repent, bending the knees of your hearts.
entries.modernizedText: You, therefore, who laid the foundation of this sedition, submit yourselves to the presbyters and receive correction so as to repent, bending the knees of your hearts.

entries.originalText: Learn to be subject, laying aside the proud and arrogant self-confidence of your tongue.
entries.modernizedText: Learn to be subject, laying aside the proud and arrogant self-confidence of your tongue.

entries.originalText: For it is better for you that ye should occupy a humble but honourable place in the flock of Christ, than that, being highly exalted, ye should be cast out from the hope of His people.
entries.modernizedText: For it is better for you to occupy a humble but honorable place in the flock of Christ than, being highly exalted, to be cast out from the hope of His people.

entries.originalText: For thus speaketh all-virtuous Wisdom: “Behold, I will bring forth to you the words of my Spirit, and I will teach you my speech.
entries.modernizedText: For thus speaks all-virtuous Wisdom: “Behold, I will bring forth to you the words of my Spirit, and I will teach you my speech.

entries.originalText: Since I called, and ye did not hear; I held forth my words, and ye regarded not, but set at naught my counsels, and yielded not at my reproofs; therefore I too will laugh at your destruction; yea, I will rejoice when ruin cometh upon you, and when sudden confusion overtakes you, when overturning presents itself like a tempest, or when tribulation and oppression fall upon you.
entries.modernizedText: Since I called and you did not hear; I held forth my words and you paid no attention, but set my counsels at naught and did not yield to my reproofs; therefore I too will laugh at your destruction. Yes, I will rejoice when ruin comes upon you, when sudden confusion overtakes you, when overturning presents itself like a tempest, or when tribulation and oppression fall upon you.

entries.originalText: For it shall come to pass, that when ye call upon me, I will not hear you; the wicked shall seek me, and they shall not find me.
entries.modernizedText: For it shall come to pass that when you call upon me, I will not hear you; the wicked shall seek me, and they shall not find me.

entries.originalText: For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the fear of the Lord; nor would they listen to my counsels, but despised my reproofs.
entries.modernizedText: For they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord; nor would they listen to my counsels, but despised my reproofs.

entries.originalText: Wherefore they shall eat the fruits of their own way, and they shall be filled with their own ungodliness.…For, in punishment for the wrongs which they practised upon babes, shall they be slain, and inquiry will be death to the ungodly; but he that heareth me shall rest in hope and be undisturbed by the fear of any evil.”
entries.modernizedText: Therefore they shall eat the fruits of their own way, and they shall be filled with their own ungodliness.…For, in punishment for the wrongs they practiced against infants, they shall be slain, and inquiry will be death to the ungodly; but he who hears me shall rest in hope and be undisturbed by the fear of any evil.”

entries.originalText: Let us, therefore, flee from the warning threats pronounced by Wisdom on the disobedient, and yield submission to His all-holy and glorious name, that we may stay our trust upon the most hallowed name of His majesty.
entries.modernizedText: Let us, therefore, flee from the warning threats pronounced by Wisdom against the disobedient, and submit to His all-holy and glorious name, that we may place our trust in the most hallowed name of His majesty.

entries.originalText: Receive our counsel, and ye shall be without repentance.
entries.modernizedText: Receive our counsel, and you shall have no cause for repentance.

entries.originalText: For, as God liveth, and as the Lord Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost live,—both the faith and hope of the elect, he who in lowliness of mind, with instant gentleness, and without repentance hath observed the ordinances and appointments given by God—the same shall obtain a place and name in the number of those who are being saved through Jesus Christ, through whom is glory to Him for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: For, as God lives, and as the Lord Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost live—the faith and hope of the elect—he who in lowliness of mind, with constant gentleness, and without repentance has observed the ordinances and appointments given by God shall obtain a place and name among those who are being saved through Jesus Christ, through whom is glory to Him forever and ever.

entries.originalText: If, however, any shall disobey the words spoken by Him through us, let them know that they will involve themselves in transgression and serious danger; but we shall be innocent of this sin, and, instant in prayer and supplication, shall desire that the Creator of all preserve unbroken the computed number of His elect in the whole world through His beloved Son Jesus Christ, through whom He called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to knowledge of the glory of His name, our hope resting on Thy name which is primal cause of every creature,—having opened the eyes of our heart to the knowledge of Thee, who alone “dost rest highest among the highest, holy among the holy,” who “layest low the insolence of the haughty,” who “destroyest the calculations of the heathen,” who “settest the low on high and bringest low the exalted;” who “makest rich and makest poor,” who “killest and makest to live,” only Benefactor of spirits and God of all flesh, who beholdest the depths, the eye-witness of human works, the help of those in danger, the Saviour of those in despair, the Creator and Guardian of every spirit, who multipliest nations upon earth, and from all madest choice of those who love Thee through Jesus Christ, Thy beloved Son, through whom Thou didst instruct, sanctify, honour us.
entries.modernizedText: If, however, any should disobey the words spoken by Him through us, let them know that they will involve themselves in transgression and serious danger; but we shall be innocent of this sin and, constant in prayer and supplication, shall desire that the Creator of all preserve unbroken the full number of His elect in the whole world through His beloved Son Jesus Christ, through whom He called us from darkness to light and from ignorance to the knowledge of the glory of His name. Our hope rests on Your name, which is the primal cause of every creature, having opened the eyes of our heart to the knowledge of You, who alone “do rest highest among the highest, holy among the holy,” who “lay low the insolence of the haughty,” who “destroy the calculations of the heathen,” who “set the low on high and bring low the exalted;” who “make rich and make poor,” who “kill and make alive,” only Benefactor of spirits and God of all flesh, who behold the depths, the eyewitness of human works, the help of those in danger, the Savior of those in despair, the Creator and Guardian of every spirit, who multiply nations upon earth, and from all make choice of those who love You through Jesus Christ, Your beloved Son, through whom You instructed, sanctified, and honored us.

entries.originalText: We would have Thee, Lord, to prove our help and succour.
entries.modernizedText: We would have You, Lord, prove our help and support.

entries.originalText: Those of us in affliction save, on the lowly take pity; the fallen raise; upon those in need arise; the sick heal; the wandering ones of Thy people turn; fill the hungry; redeem those of us in bonds; raise up those that are weak; comfort the faint-hearted; let all the nations know that Thou art God alone and Jesus Christ Thy Son, and we are Thy people and the sheep of Thy pasture.
entries.modernizedText: Save those of us in affliction; take pity on the lowly; raise the fallen; rise up for those in need; heal the sick; turn back the wandering ones of Your people; fill the hungry; redeem those of us in bonds; raise up those who are weak; comfort the faint-hearted; let all the nations know that You are God alone and Jesus Christ Your Son, and that we are Your people and the sheep of Your pasture.

entries.originalText: Thou didst make to appear the enduring fabric of the world by the works of Thy hand; Thou, Lord, didst create the earth on which we dwell,—Thou, who art faithful in all generations, just in judgments, wonderful in strength and majesty, with wisdom creating and with understanding fixing the things which were made, who art good among them that are being saved and faithful among them whose trust is in Thee; O merciful and Compassionate One, forgive us our iniquities and offences and transgressions and trespasses.
entries.modernizedText: You made the enduring fabric of the world appear through the works of Your hand; You, Lord, created the earth on which we dwell—You who are faithful in all generations, just in judgments, wonderful in strength and majesty, creating with wisdom and fixing with understanding the things that were made, who are good among those who are being saved and faithful among those whose trust is in You. O merciful and compassionate One, forgive us our iniquities, offenses, transgressions, and trespasses.

entries.originalText: Reckon not every sin of Thy servants and handmaids, but Thou wilt purify us with the purification of Thy truth; and direct our steps that we may walk in holiness of heart and do what is good and well-pleasing in Thy sight and in the sight of our rulers.
entries.modernizedText: Do not reckon every sin of Your servants and handmaids, but purify us with the purification of Your truth; and direct our steps so that we may walk in holiness of heart and do what is good and pleasing in Your sight and in the sight of our rulers.

entries.originalText: Yea, Lord, make Thy face to shine upon us for good in peace, that we may be shielded by Thy mighty hand and delivered from every sin by Thine uplifted arm, and deliver us from those who hate us wrongfully.
entries.modernizedText: Yes, Lord, make Your face shine upon us for good in peace, so that we may be shielded by Your mighty hand and delivered from every sin by Your uplifted arm, and deliver us from those who hate us wrongfully.

entries.originalText: Give concord and peace to us and all who dwell upon the earth, even as Thou gavest to our fathers, when they called upon Thee in faith and truth, submissive as we are to Thine almighty and all-excellent Name.
entries.modernizedText: Give concord and peace to us and all who dwell upon the earth, just as You gave them to our fathers when they called upon You in faith and truth, as we submit to Your almighty and all-excellent Name.

entries.originalText: To our rulers and governors on the earth—to them Thou, Lord, gavest the power of the kingdom by Thy glorious and ineffable might, to the end that we may know the glory and honour given to them by Thee and be subject to them, in nought resisting Thy will; to them, Lord, give health, peace, concord, stability, that they may exercise the authority given to them without offence.
entries.modernizedText: To our rulers and governors on the earth—to them You, Lord, gave the power of the kingdom by Your glorious and ineffable might, so that we may know the glory and honor given to them by You and be subject to them, resisting Your will in nothing. To them, Lord, give health, peace, concord, and stability, that they may exercise the authority given to them without offense.

entries.originalText: For Thou, O heavenly Lord and King eternal, givest to the sons of men glory and honour and power over the things that are on the earth; do Thou, Lord, direct their counsel according to that which is good and well-pleasing in Thy sight, that, devoutly in peace and meekness exercising the power given them by Thee, they may find Thee propitious.
entries.modernizedText: For You, O heavenly Lord and eternal King, give the sons of men glory, honor, and power over the things that are on the earth; direct their counsel, Lord, according to what is good and pleasing in Your sight, so that, devoutly exercising in peace and meekness the power given them by You, they may find You favorable.

entries.originalText: O Thou, who only hast power to do these things and more abundant good with us, we praise Thee through the High Priest and Guardian of our souls Jesus Christ, through whom be glory and majesty to Thee both now and from generation to generation and for evermore.
entries.modernizedText: O You who alone have power to do these things and greater good for us, we praise You through the High Priest and Guardian of our souls, Jesus Christ, through whom be glory and majesty to You both now and from generation to generation and forevermore.

entries.originalText: Concerning the things pertaining to our religious observance which are most profitable for a life of goodness to those who would pursue a godly and righteous course, we have written to you, men and brethren, at sufficient length.
entries.modernizedText: Concerning the things pertaining to our religious observance that are most profitable for a life of goodness to those who would pursue a godly and righteous course, we have written to you, men and brethren, at sufficient length.

entries.originalText: For concerning faith and repentance and true love and continence and soberness and patience, we have touched upon every passage, putting you in mind that you ought in righteousness and truth and long-suffering to be well-pleasing to Almighty God with holiness, being of one mind—not remembering evil—in love and peace with instant gentleness, even as also our fathers forementioned found favour by the humility of their thoughts towards the Father and God and Creator and all mankind.
entries.modernizedText: For concerning faith, repentance, true love, self-control, sobriety, and patience, we have touched upon every subject, reminding you that in righteousness, truth, and patience you ought to be pleasing to Almighty God with holiness, being of one mind—not remembering evil—in love and peace with constant gentleness, just as our aforementioned fathers also found favor through the humility of their thoughts toward the Father, God, Creator, and all mankind.

entries.originalText: And of these things we put you in mind with the greater pleasure, since we were well assured that we were writing to men who were faithful and of highest repute and had peered into the oracles of the instruction of God.
entries.modernizedText: And we remind you of these things with even greater pleasure, since we were well assured that we were writing to men who were faithful, of the highest repute, and had examined the oracles of God’s instruction.

entries.originalText: Right is it, therefore, to approach examples so good and so many, and submit the neck and fulfil the part of obedience, in order that, undisturbed by vain sedition, we may attain unto the goal set before us in truth wholly free from blame.
entries.modernizedText: It is right, therefore, to approach such good and numerous examples, submit the neck, and fulfill the duty of obedience, so that, undisturbed by vain sedition, we may attain the goal set before us in truth, wholly free from blame.

entries.originalText: Joy and gladness will ye afford us, if ye become obedient to the words written by us and through the Holy Spirit root out the lawless wrath of your jealousy according to the intercession which we have made for peace and unity in this letter.
entries.modernizedText: You will bring us joy and gladness if you become obedient to the words written by us and, through the Holy Spirit, root out the lawless wrath of your jealousy according to the intercession we have made for peace and unity in this letter.

entries.originalText: We have sent men faithful and discreet, whose conversation from youth to old age has been blameless amongst us,—the same shall be witnesses between you and us.
entries.modernizedText: We have sent faithful and discreet men, whose conduct from youth to old age has been blameless among us; they shall be witnesses between you and us.

entries.originalText: This we have done, that ye may know that our whole concern has been and is that ye may be speedily at peace.
entries.modernizedText: We have done this so that you may know that our whole concern has been and is that you may quickly be at peace.

entries.originalText: May God, who seeth all things, and who is the Ruler of all spirits and the Lord of all flesh—who chose our Lord Jesus Christ and us through Him to be a peculiar people—grant to every soul that calleth upon His glorious and holy name, faith, fear, peace, patience, long-suffering, self-control, purity, and sobriety, to the well-pleasing of His name, through our High Priest and Protector, Jesus Christ, by whom be to Him glory, and majesty, and power, and honour, both now and for evermore.
entries.modernizedText: May God, who sees all things and who is the Ruler of all spirits and the Lord of all flesh—who chose our Lord Jesus Christ and us through Him to be a special people—grant to every soul that calls upon His glorious and holy name faith, fear, peace, patience, long-suffering, self-control, purity, and sobriety, pleasing to His name, through our High Priest and Protector, Jesus Christ, by whom be glory, majesty, power, and honor to Him both now and forevermore.

entries.originalText: Send back speedily to us in peace and with joy these our messengers to you: Claudius Ephebus and Valerius Bito, with Fortunatus; that they may the sooner announce to us the peace and harmony we so earnestly desire and long for [among you], and that we may the more quickly rejoice over the good order re-established among you.
entries.modernizedText: Send back quickly to us in peace and with joy these messengers of ours to you: Claudius Ephebus and Valerius Bito, with Fortunatus, so that they may sooner announce to us the peace and harmony we so earnestly desire and long for [among you], and so that we may more quickly rejoice over the good order reestablished among you.

entries.originalText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you, and with all everywhere that are the called of God through Him, by whom be to Him glory, honour, power, majesty, and eternal dominion, from everlasting to everlasting.
entries.modernizedText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you and with all everywhere who are called by God through Him, by whom be glory, honor, power, majesty, and eternal dominion to Him, from everlasting to everlasting.
